Posted February 18, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

It is important to understand that in the fable about the Emperor's New Clothes everyone knew that the emperor was in his skivvies, they were just afraid to say so.

What they feared was not the emperor's police, but the scorn of their peers for not being able to see what wasn't there. When the little boy, who was too young to be thus inhibited, spoke the truth, everyone was freed from the common lie.

The first reason for my revisiting this old story is to make the point that the people who pretended to see what was not there, or not to see what was, are like today's reporters and editors. Many of them know perfectly well that they can see parts of the Emperor that they had just as soon not see, but if they write about it, they fear that their careers will be damaged. I have had reporters and editors tell me just that, and this is one reason why the media are so distrusted.

What do you do when All the news that fits doesn't fit anymore?
See
Negligent Journalism: Reader Beware or A Right to Expect More? The Drug Czar Says He Is Subject to the Scrutiny of the Press. The Significance of the Ultimate Lies. Analysis by Richard Cowan

The second reason for revisiting the fable is to make the point that the little boy's candor did not create what is called a paradigm shift. That term has become something of a cliché without really being understood. That lack of understanding may be central to the nature of the phenomenon.

The best simple illustration of a paradigm shift is found in the drawing, which, when seen one way is a beautiful young woman, and when seen in another way is an old crone. When someone finally sees the other picture that was there all along, that is the paradigm shift.

The simplest equivalent of a paradigm shift in the cannabis debate would be the understanding that the gateway between cannabis and hard drugs is not inherent in cannabis, but in cannabis prohibition. The facts remain the same, but the understanding changes things utterly.
See
The Gateway Theory Won't Die Because It Tells Prohibitionists Something They Want to Believe, But The Truth Tells Them Something They Refuse to Hear.


A more recent example may be found in the new prohibitionist party line that seeks to connect drug use and the violence of prohibition, or with terrorism. When the connection is seen to be prohibition and not the drugs, that is a shift in perception, although the facts remain the same.
See
Did The Drug War Claim Another 3,056 Casualties On 9-11? Ariana Huffington's Extraordinary Indictment.
and
The Endless Cynicism of the Drug Warriors. The Drug War and Terrorism. MarijuanaNews Analysis by Richard Cowan

The ultimate paradigm shift will occur, when as a result of the cumulative effect of destroying the components of prohibitionist propaganda the focus of the debate shifts from the truth about cannabis, to the lies about cannabis.

The truth about cannabis is important for individuals to know, so that they can make personal decisions about its use, but the lies about cannabis tell us something profoundly important about how we govern ourselves and the danger that governmental lying poses to our freedom.
See
They've Lied to Us About Marijuana, So How Do We Know That They Aren't Lying About Iraq? Credibility in Time of War.
and
Dan Forbes Documents Walters Lies About Potency. Understanding That The War On Cannabis Is Built On Lies Is Key to Understanding More Than Just Drug War.

That is a political question at its most fundamental, and any shift in perception into what is happening will be the paradigm shift that ultimately destroys cannabis prohibition and the whole drug war. That last point, the danger to the broader drug war, may also be a catalyst to changing the status of medical cannabis.

Recently, the New York Times editorialized against the Bush/Walters/Ashcroft war on the sick and dying, not from any great humanitarian perspective, but rather to say that the narks time would be better spent elsewhere, the administration should stop tyrannizing doctors and sick people and focus on more important aspects of the war on drugs.
See
Astonishing Editorial In New York Times Attacks Rosenthal Prosecution. Finally Taking The Issue Seriously?

These moderates are trying to save the drug war from the drug warriors. Lots a luck. The fact that the drug war is being driven by fanatics like John Walters makes such a pragmatic change in strategy all but impossible, and the cultural gulf between the pragmatists and the fundamentalist drug warriors grows wider every day.
See
The Police Fraud. Someone Is Lying. Marking The 30th Anniversary Of An Article in National Review. What if Don Quixote Was Right? Analysis by Richard Cowan

That is a realpolitik conclusion that is not apt to go over well with the reefer madness crowd that makes up the hard core constituency of the drug war, the nutcases that show up to protest state bills that would allow a university agriculture school to study the possibility of thinking about considering researching the concept of the feasibility of growing hemp, because it would send the wrong message to children that crack cocaine is good for you.
See
Letter to The Washington Post From Drug Watch/Minnesota
Should Teach The " Me No Marijuana " Hemp Promoters
That Trying to Distance Themselves From Marijuana Reform Will Not Stop The Lying


Polls consistently show that opposition to cannabis prohibition rises with income and education levels. It is also higher among young people, and on the West Coast, where trends usually begin. These are the demographics that are most sought after by both advertisers and political analysts.

These early adapters are still inhibited from saying what they know, like the emperor's cynical subjects, because they are afraid of being thought of as pro-drug or worse yet, being suspected of being closet smokers, which they often are.

(In the fable, the emperor did not employ narks. He was a fool, but not a knave, unlike the appalling people who govern us, so the analogy is not precise.)

However, in the real world, as people see through one illusion lie after another, they eventually connect the dots and have their epiphany, their paradigm shift, and understand that the lies are the issue.

This was beautifully illustrated in an extraordinary letter by an ordinary American published in the Watertown, New York, Daily Times. The author clearly gets it and so makes his points with mordant wit. This gentleman not only says that the emperor is underdressed, he mocks those who for venal reasons pretend other wise.

If the media have a credibility problem now, think what it will be like when the reality that cannabis prohibition is a counterproductive fraud becomes the new paradigm.
See
The Washington Post and The Evil of Banality. " Only the hypocrite is really rotten to the core.

From The Watertown Daily Times

By Robert K. Kirchoff
February 15, 2003

Anti-Drug Commercial Sends Wrong Message

There is a new anti-drug campaign television commercial that has a young man clumsily defending his purchase of illegal drugs against an older man. This older man declares that drug money supports terrorism. Is this what the feds expect me to think.

Were the 9-11 hijacking murderers financed oil-wealthy individuals and nations or by the narcotics underworld? Were the 9-11 terrorist allowed to roam the U.S. through failure to enforce immigration laws or the drug laws?

How are/were known terrorist able to freely and frequently cross the border where peaceful citizens are turned away because they are behind in child support payments?

How were the 9-11 terrorist able to move large sums of money without notice, which is something, no American citizen can do? For all its failings, was not the Taliban strongly anti-drug and in the process of eradicating the poppy fields of Afghanistan?

The small pox and anthrax possessed by Iraq was sold with the permission of the federal government ( maybe there is a drugs fry our brain link after all ). The Iraqi nuclear program came from Europe, in particular the centrifuges and related enrichment technology from Germany. Plastic explosives used by terrorist don't come from anyone's garage either.

Are these weapons and poisons created and " controlled " by drug cartels or governments? Were the purchases of these products done by drug lords or by governments through taxation of the citizenry? Was the distribution of these products and the potential dangers discussed with the citizenry? And was permission to do so sought?

No, of course not! We, the citizens, have to deal with such recklessness committed " on our behalf " by faceless, unaccountable government. It's as though a child were to say, " by the way Dad, I left that smallpox stuff with Saddam-oops! "

So the message of this particular anti-drug commercial is clear to me: the federal government is not to be blamed for any part of the current mess: we, the people are to blame.

No one at the federal level is to be held accountable. Neither incompetence, nor failure to enforce just laws, nor the continued refusal of the elite who rule us ( as opposed to governing ) to heed the wise voices of the founders of this republic have caused the American people harm. No sir! Indeed, and with certainty, it's the guy next door smoking pot who is about to destroy our way of life.

ROBERT K. KIRCHOFF

Clayton
